key_highlights: ASX ended a volatile week higher despite Wall Street retreat and Fed hawkish commentary on inflation (10, 52)
Aussie interest rate expectations rocket, signalling potential RBA hawkish shift; mortgage rates rising week-on-week (36, 38)
Housing market under stress: auction sentiment deteriorating, signs of a 'real housing crash' emerging (42, 59, 64)
US strikes on Iranian launchers in Strait of Hormuz elevate geopolitical risk and oil price volatility (6, 66)
Pilbara iron ore 'killer' booms; Gateway Resources adds 7km gold trend in WA; small-caps X2M, Discovery Alaska, Metal Hawk, Bapcor lead ASX runners (57, 62, 54)
ASIC warns insurers short-changing homeowners on cash settlements, creating regulatory overhang for insurance sector (15, 24, 32)
Virgin Australia shielded from oil shock via fuel hedging and new fleet (58)
Consumer trends: surging weight-loss drug demand, 'dupe' brand loyalty, accelerating EV uptake (44)

sectors.trend: Positive. Pilbara iron ore production surging ('killer booms'), Gateway Resources discovers 7km gold trend in WA. Small-cap miners (X2M, Discovery Alaska, Metal Hawk, Bapcor) lead weekly gains. Geopolitical tension in Hormuz supports commodity prices.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from iron ore strength. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NGX.AX) supported by safe-haven flows from Iran conflict. Small-cap explorers see speculative inflows.

sectors.trend: Mixed-to-negative. Rising rate expectations (36) support NIMs but housing stress (42, 59, 64) raises credit-loss concerns. Mortgage rates climbing week-on-week (38). ASIC scrutiny of insurers pressures IAG.AX, CGF.AX.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face a tug-of-war: higher yields vs. deteriorating housing credit quality. Insurers (IAG.AX, CGF.AX) face regulatory and reputational risk from settlement practices.

sectors.trend: Elevated volatility. US-Iran conflict in Strait of Hormuz (6) spikes oil risk premium. Virgin Australia (QAN.AX) insulated via hedging (58). Oil majors retreating from clean energy capex (16). Australia sets 'high bar' for fossil-fuel-powered data centres (53).
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, SXG.AX benefit from oil price spikes. QAN.AX neutral-to-positive on hedging. Renewable/energy-transition names face policy headwinds from data-centre restrictions.

sectors.trend: Divergent. Weight-loss drug demand surging, EV uptake accelerating, 'dupe' brands gaining share (44). Major fruit grower lays off ~1,000 workers (41). Qantas redundancies signal labour-market softening (61).
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, WES.AX, WOW.AX see mixed signals. CSL benefits from global weight-loss drug demand. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) supported by 'dupe' trend. QAN.AX faces ongoing restructuring overhang.

sectors.trend: AI power demand transforming industrials into high-multiple plays (31). SpaceX potential disruption to AI data centres (47). Australia restricts fossil-fuel data centres (53).
sectors.implications: ASX-listed data-centre and power infrastructure names (e.g., VMC.AX, IAG.AX infrastructure) benefit. Energy demand tailwind for utilities. Regulatory constraints may favour renewables.

sectors.trend: Negative. Housing auction sentiment deteriorating (42), signs of a genuine housing crash (59), households being terminated (64). Housing inflation persistent (60).
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICOL.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Residential property developers (SRG.AX, MYR.AX) at elevated risk. Mortgage-backed securities under stress.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile. Hormuz conflict and Fed hawkishness cap upside, but commodity strength (iron ore, gold, oil) and a resilient week-close (52) provide a floor. Rate-expectation spike (36) pressures rate-sensitive sectors. Net: range-bound with sector rotation into materials and energy.
market_outlook.long_term: Housing correction risk (59, 64) and persistent housing inflation (60) constrain RBA easing, keeping rates elevated. AI-driven power demand (31, 47) and commodity super-cycle in iron ore/gold support structural earnings growth. Consumer shift to 'dupe' brands and weight-loss drugs (44) reshapes retail and pharma. 12-month view: cautious constructive, favouring materials, energy, and healthcare over property and consumer discretionary.
